Alex: Heads up — ~09:12 UTC p99 spike on api-prod-1. Noticed KV prefix hit-rate collapse on shard g12 (92% -> 18%) right after the rolling deploy that enabled adaptive-kernel-scheduler + prefetch_pulse. Latency from dashboards: p50 +8ms, p95 +40ms, p99 +230ms. Link: https://dash.redwood/prod/api-prod-1 :eyes:
Maya: I see it too. Dashboards show eviction_rate jumped ~60x. Any config changes besides the kernel flag?
Alex: Only the kernel flag and prefetch_pulse=true on the deploy. Logs look noisy — here's a small extract from the runtime logs around the deploy:
```
2026-03-18T09:11:54Z kernel-selector: selected quant_fast for model:open-enc-6 seq=64
2026-03-18T09:11:54Z prefetcher: pulse start shard=g12 tenant=acme ttl=120
2026-03-18T09:11:55Z kv-cache: evict candidate count=12432
2026-03-18T09:12:03Z kernel-selector: selected gcc_opt for model:open-enc-6 seq=16
```
PerfBot: Perf summary (automated): p99_latency: 48ms -> 278ms, kv_prefix_hitrate_shard_g12: 0.92 -> 0.18, eviction_rate_per_min: 0.2 -> 12.1, affected_replicas: 6
Jonah: I pulled a heap/profile and a small mapping sample. Looks like the kernel path is mutating the prefix key format in the hot path. Keys used to be canonical_prefix = model|tenant|prefixhash; new quant_fast path appends a kernel_marker `#Q` to the in-memory key before hashing, which the prefetcher also writes. That means prefetch primes keys that the primary cache lookup doesn't match (or worse — overwrites different canonical entries). Example:
```
old_key: open-enc-6|acme|pfx_0a3f
new_key_written_by_prefetch: open-enc-6|acme|pfx_0a3f#Q
lookup_from_serving_path: open-enc-6|acme|pfx_0a3f
```
Sasha: If prefetch writes `#Q` variants with TTL=120s and the lookup path expects no marker, that's effectively cache poisoning / duplication and primes a bunch of entries that won't be used, while evicting the canonical ones. Also seen misrouted prefetch bursts — prefetcher sometimes sends priming to wrong shard due to a scheduler misroute when kernel selection changes the computed shard key.
Emily: Rolling rollback of adaptive-kernel-scheduler and prefetch_pulse on g12 now (manually toggled flag to false). Observing canary of 2 machines: kv_prefix_hitrate rising from 18% -> ~80% on the canary hosts after ~2 minutes.
Alex: Good. But we need a permanent fix. My notes: two independent-but-compounding bugs — (1) kernel path should not mutate prefix key material used for caching, any kernel-specific marker must be metadata-only, (2) prefetch scheduler should use canonical_prefix() for shard routing and priming writes.
Maya: I'll open a follow-up ticket with reproducer, flamegraphs, and exact deploy ids. Early repro steps to include in ticket:
- run mixed seqlen workload (seq 8/32/64) against model open-enc-6
- enable adaptive-kernel-scheduler + prefetch_pulse
- observe prefetch writes containing kernel markers and mis-sharded priming bursts
- capture kv eviction traces and hash samples
Jonah: Proposed patch: change kernel-selector to set kernel metadata in request context rather than append to prefix key; update prefetcher to call canonical_prefix(request) for both writes and shard computation; add unit tests that validate canonicalization and a small integration test that prime/lookup keys are identical across kernel paths. I'll draft a PR.
PerfBot: Alert cleared on shard g12 after rollback. key_metrics: kv_prefix_hitrate_shard_g12 0.18 -> 0.87 within 4m. New ticket created: RUNTIME-6557 (adaptive-kernel-prefetch-keying-regression).
Emily: Thanks team. Let's capture full flamegraphs + alloc profiles for postmortem. Postmortem scheduled tomorrow 16:00 UTC. Please attach: deploy ids, exact flag toggles, metric deltas, and the small log snippet that shows prefetch writes with `#Q`.
Alex: Agreed. Also add a short doc on safe key metadata practices so kernel authors don't accidentally bake metadata into hashable keys again. :memo:
